missionPremise: Eleven domains have been registered, deterministic and served at GET /api/domains/<id> since G-91, and they reached NO pixel. Ruling 1 (operator-approved 2026-08-19, OPS-17 A-081) says the four source states are four different customer sentences and that collapsing any pair re-creates the defect the ruling exists to close. Until a lens rendered them, ruling 1 was implemented in src/fixture-seam.mjs and invisible to every customer - four waves built everything underneath the lenses and never the lenses, which is the deferral A-081 records against the planner. This lane makes two of the fifteen lenses show it. Sources: OPS-17 A-081 and A-080; src/fixture-seam.mjs DOMAIN_STATUSES and its own comment on why the four cannot collapse.
completionPredicate: A stranger opens /?lens=fleet and /?lens=public-works on template-city and sees generated records with their counting rules and their basis lines; opens both on ?cityKey=empty-city and sees every region reachable, quiet, and stating why it is empty; and is shown ungranted and granted-empty rendering as two visibly different sentences on the same regions. CI conclusion string is "success", the suite count has not fallen, and axe on both themes on both surfaces adds zero nodes to color-contrast and zero to scrollable-region-focusable while heading-order does not grow. Every one of those is evidenced below with raw output.
scopeBasis: The dispatch assigned exactly the two <section> blocks and the CSS they need. Sibling lanes R1 (Development services) and R2 (Police, Fire and EMS) hold disjoint sections of the same two files from separate clones, so anything shared was touched append-only and no other lens was edited. web/app.js was NOT in the ownership sentence and was unavoidable: a composed payload reaches a browser only through a served script, and the dispatch's own instruction was to compose the existing seam rather than write a second data path. That change is one contiguous appended block plus two boot lines. web/shell.css and web/sc-kit.css were not edited AT ALL - measured, 0 diff lines against main. OUT and why: the nav badge markup and the Overview 'Across departments' register both carry claims this lane falsifies and both sit outside the two sections; they are reported under openItems rather than reached into. The kit token defect this lane surfaced is cross-repo and belongs to a G-94-shaped lane. Live Bastrop untouched and unread. G-52 not started. G-24 held at zero. L26 untouched.

findings.title: the accessibility gate's coverage is bounded by the viewport: a conformance defect below the fold of a scrollable column is not reported
findings.howItWasFound: CP2 left a reconciliation open - Development services renders two p-ok pills, the pair computes to 4.44:1, and neither the local scanner nor the merged CI gate reported a node on that surface. Two numbers that should agree and did not.
findings.settled: by scanning the SAME surface at two viewport heights. Raw: 'DS 900px (rows below the fold) violations=[] visible p-ok pills=2' and 'DS 3000px (all rows inside the fold) violations=[{"id":"color-contrast","nodes":2}]'. The pills are present and visible in both runs; only the viewport differs.
findings.consequence: '0 conformance nodes over 46 scans' is true AT 1440x900 rather than absolutely. It also explains this lane's own earlier partial number - 6 of 8 in-service pills were reported, the last two sat past the fold - so the same bound was visible in my data before it was understood.
findings.notADefectInThisLane: the finding argues for MORE coverage, not less: my surfaces are clean at both 900px and 3000px, measured, because they render no p-ok pill at all.
findings.plannerAction: route to the accessibility lane. A second viewport height, or scrolling each scrollable region through its full extent, would close it. Named rather than fixed here because the gate is G-95's and reaching into it from a rendering lane is how two implementations of one rule start.
